flags.detail: data/desk/correlations.json publishes r = -0.161 labelled 'game total vs |margin|', n = 137, reading 'same-game total and blowout size move together'. requirements.acceptance: For every originated market there is one row per book carrying market_id, book, open_price, open_timestamp, close_price, close_timestamp, price_format and source_url. A market cannot be graded unless open and close are both present.
requirements.blocker: No price provider. The store is waiting on a data-rights decision, not on code. See Q01 and S01.
requirements.evidence_label: repo artifact - schema live, prices blank
requirements.status_text: Store is live with schema origin-snapshots-v1, append-only by (market_id, phase): 39 open rows RECORDED, 39 close rows PENDING. Every market_line is blank, so no closing-line value can be computed yet.
requirements.title: Price-snapshot store that records opening and closing numbers for every market we originate
requirements.why: Without both ends of the price, closing-line value cannot be measured, and without closing-line value a hit rate is not evidence of skill.

requirements.acceptance: One row per completed game with final score for both clubs, the official source URL, the retrieval timestamp, and a written settlement rule per market type (side, total, moneyline) including how ties and pushes are treated.
requirements.blocker: No settlement rule, and no player-prop results. See Q04, S02, S09.
requirements.evidence_label: repo artifact - transcription of official week pages
requirements.owner: origin/data/results.json and origin/data/backtest.json (session arena/f2df8317-x3, merged in PR #47); data/desk/games.json (session arena/3bf7cc8b-x3)
requirements.status_text: The feed exists and backtests now run on it: origin/data/results.json holds 163 games / 137 finals with a per-row official URL, cross-checked 163/163 against the desk game log, and a walk-forward backtest is published per week. ROI still cannot be computed, and no settlement rule is written down.
requirements.title: Verified results feed so backtests and ROI can be computed at all
requirements.why: ROI is (settled return - stake) / stake. Every term needs a settled result, so without a results feed no leaderboard row can be scored.

requirements.acceptance: Each game carries three originated rows in the order side, total, moneyline. The moneyline row records the margin and the sigma it was derived from, so it is reproducible.
requirements.blocker: None. The order requirement is satisfied.
requirements.evidence_label: repo artifact - order verified 0 violations of 13
requirements.status_text: 39 originated rows, 13 games x 3 market types, with seq order side then total then moneyline. This session re-checked the order for all 13 games: 0 violations. The moneyline records its own derivation - P(home win) = Phi(adj_margin / 13.5) on the side's adjusted margin - so it is reproducible from the side.
requirements.title: Originate the side first, then the total, then the moneyline
requirements.why: The moneyline is a function of the expected margin and its uncertainty. Deriving it last keeps the three markets mutually consistent; deriving them independently produces arbitrage against yourself.

requirements.acceptance: Three distinct columns per market: fair_line, market_line, and edge = fair_line - market_line, each with its own units label and sign convention.
requirements.blocker: Depends on R1. No official source publishes NFL prices. See Q01 and S01.
requirements.evidence_label: repo artifact - columns present, market and diff blank
requirements.status_text: The column contract exists: fair_line, market_line and diff are three separate fields on all 39 rows, each with a unit label and a recorded sign convention. fair_line is populated for every market. market_line and diff are blank in all 39 rows because no source publishes a price.
requirements.title: Publish the model's fair line, the market line, and the difference as separate columns
requirements.why: The difference is the whole signal. Publishing only a fair line leaves the reader to do the subtraction against a price they cannot see.

requirements.acceptance: Every leaderboard row carries two independently computed scores: a signal score that is stake-independent (mean closing-line value per bet, with n and a 95% CI) and a staking score that is PnL-dependent (ROI, drawdown, units). A strategy must be able to rank top-decile on signal while flat on staking, and the board must show both columns.
requirements.blocker: The staking half needs prices and a settlement rule. See Q01, Q04, S05.
requirements.evidence_label: repo artifact - signal populated, staking blocked
requirements.status_text: The separation is implemented in the data rather than only described: every leaderboard row carries a signal block (metric, value, n, rank) and a separate staking block. The signal half is populated - side winner-direction accuracy 0.595 (n = 121), total over/under hit rate 0.4957 (n = 117), moneyline Brier 0.2373 (n = 121). The staking half is blocked with 0 settled bets.
requirements.title: Separate 'signal' from 'staking' in the leaderboard so a lucky staking run cannot mask a bad signal
requirements.why: A flat-stake record measures whether the fair line was right. A sized record mixes that with how much was risked. Ranking on the blend lets a Kelly run on coin-flips outrank a real edge.

requirements.acceptance: For each absent starter: the ordinal depth of the replacement (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th string or undrafted/free-agent pickup), the club chart URL, and the chart's as-of date. A row without an as-of date is published as unverified, not as fact.
requirements.blocker: No chart carries a date, so an ordinal cannot be tied to a point in time. See Q06, S06, S07, and flag C-12 for a count discrepancy between the two trees.
requirements.evidence_label: repo artifact - club charts, no as-of date
requirements.owner: origin/data/depth.json (session arena/f2df8317-x3, merged in PR #47); data/desk/deficiencies.json (session arena/3bf7cc8b-x3)
requirements.status_text: An ordinal is now recorded, not just a name: replacement_ordinal is populated for 42 of 76 Week 10 absences, with a reason_if_blank field explaining each gap. Zero of 76 rows carry a chart as-of date, and the club charts are self-labelled unofficial by the clubs that publish them.
requirements.title: Track the depth of the replacement, not just the fact of a replacement
requirements.why: 'Starter out' and 'third-string guard starting' are different events with different expected effects. Counting only the fact treats them as identical and throws away the signal.

requirements.acceptance: Every published coefficient carries n, the official source URL, a 95% CI, and a plain reading. A coefficient whose CI contains 0 is labelled 'not distinguishable from no relationship' and is not used to price anything.
requirements.blocker: None. See flag C-01 for the stale copy still published on another tree.
requirements.evidence_label: repo artifact - n and CI published with every value
requirements.owner: origin/data/correlations.json (session arena/f2df8317-x3, merged in PR #47); data/desk/correlations.json (stale copy)
requirements.status_text: Every coefficient carries n, a 95% interval, and the official source URL, and the mislabelled pair has been republished correctly: game total vs |home margin| is now -0.0157 and signed home margin vs total is -0.1607, as two separate rows. The older desk copy still carries the wrong label - see flag C-01.
requirements.title: Compute correlations only from officially sourced numbers and publish n with each value
requirements.why: A correlation is the input to the parlay leg screen. An r with no n is unfalsifiable, and an r computed on unlogged data is a guess dressed as a measurement.

requirements.acceptance: A written rule with numeric thresholds, a look-back window, and an automatic action: for example, return to paper when the rolling 200-bet closing-line value is negative, or when the 95% CI on ROI contains zero over the last 200 graded bets, or on any data provenance failure. Every demotion is logged with its trigger.
requirements.blocker: None on the rule. Enforcement is still manual - see Q14 and S04.
requirements.evidence_label: repo artifact - D-1 triggers and D-2 re-promotion
requirements.status_text: Gate D-1 is written with five numeric triggers and an automatic action: rolling median closing-line value of the last 20 settled bets <= 0 twice in a row (D-1a); drawdown from peak >= 25% (D-1b); signal below 50% for three consecutive cycles (D-1c); any data-integrity failure (D-1d); any unregistered model change (D-1e). D-1d and D-1e are armed now; D-1a to D-1c arm at promotion. D-2 defines re-promotion.
requirements.title: Define a demotion gate that sends a live strategy back to paper
requirements.why: A promotion gate with no demotion gate is a one-way door: a strategy that was lucky once stays live forever. The demotion rule is what makes the promotion rule mean anything.

suggestions.effort: Path (c): an hour. Paths (a) and (b): a procurement or legal step plus a pipeline.

suggestions.proposal: Decide the price source before building more on top of it. Three paths: (a) buy a historical odds licence and ingest it in CI; (b) run the GitHub Actions runner on a schedule to snapshot one public book's board at a fixed time each day and retain only what is needed for closing-line value; (c) declare prices out of scope and re-scope the site to model accuracy against results, dropping every ROI and leaderboard claim.
suggestions.risk: Path (b) risks a terms-of-use problem and a single-book bias. Path (a) costs money. Path (c) removes the competition half of the brief.

suggestions.risk: Low. More data is strictly better here.

suggestions.evidence: Gate G4 specifies Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.10 with no test count registered (Q10).
suggestions.proposal: Preregister the number of strategy tests before testing. FDR control needs a denominator, and an unbounded search space makes any correction meaningless.
suggestions.risk: Registering too few tests and then testing more is the failure mode; log additions.

suggestions.effort: Large, and mostly legal rather than technical.
suggestions.evidence: Nothing is configured; the site already states it does not promise rewards (Q12).
suggestions.proposal: Keep rewards out of the research system. If a competition is wanted, design it as a separate surface with its own rules and its own review, and do not let prize structure feed back into the signal scores.
suggestions.risk: Contest design is regulated. This is not a legal-advice surface; get a review.

suggestions.effort: Medium: a decision plus a one-time archive move.
suggestions.evidence: Fifteen trees exist; a sixteenth is being built now (Q15).
suggestions.proposal: Stop adding duplicate site trees. Declare one canonical tree, freeze the rest as an archive, and require new work to land as pages inside the canonical tree instead of as a new root directory. This session is not exempt from the criticism: council/ is the sixteenth tree. It is additive rather than duplicative - it holds no table that another tree already publishes - but the count still went up, and a reviewer should read that as part of the problem rather than as a solution to it.
suggestions.risk: Freezing the wrong tree loses the newest registers. Check which tree holds them first.

suggestions.effort: Medium: re-fetch and re-verify, page by page.
suggestions.evidence: This session read nfl.com schedule, standings and injury pages directly and matched 50 injury rows field by field (V08, Q16).
suggestions.proposal: Correct the standing claim that the authoring environment cannot reach nfl.com, and re-run every blank table against the official pages. Several blanks are fetchable, not unknowable.
suggestions.risk: None. It only removes false blanks.

suggestions.effort: Small. The pattern already exists in scripts/audit_all.py.
suggestions.evidence: A repo-wide link and source-row gate exists, but prior sessions report 658 published rows that carry neither a link nor a flag.
suggestions.proposal: Add one gate that refuses to publish a numeric cell unless it carries either an official source URL or an explicit UNVERIFIED badge. Enforce it in CI on every tree, not only on the tree that happens to own the newest page.
suggestions.risk: Low. It makes blanks visible instead of hiding them.

suggestions.evidence: All 13 originated rows already carry empty market fields (V11, V12).
suggestions.proposal: Publish the fair, market and difference columns even while the market column is empty: three headers, two blanks, and a cell that says why. The column contract is then in place when prices arrive.
suggestions.risk: Low, provided the blanks stay visibly blank.
suggestions.status: IMPLEMENTED by origin/ (PR #47) - fair_line, market_line and diff are separate fields on all 39 rows; market and diff stay blank until prices exist.

suggestions.evidence: Walk-forward MAE 10.52, r 0.20, n 121, with no baseline published (V10, Q18).
suggestions.proposal: Report model accuracy against a published naive baseline (home team by a fixed margin, or last week's spread) so 'MAE 10.52' has something to be better than.
suggestions.risk: Low. It may show the model is not yet better than the baseline, which is useful to know.

suggestions.evidence: A prior session published a false 'standings lag the finished game' flag purely because no cut-off was recorded anywhere.
suggestions.proposal: Adopt an as-of contract for every dataset: each file declares the week, the retrieval timestamp and the source URL in the data itself, so no reader has to infer a cut-off.
